en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, West Cape May, Cape May County, New Jersey, 1890, Sheet 17

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 of the 1890 Sanborn map of Cape May, covering part of West Cape May, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left. Broadway runs across the middle of the sheet. On its east side (above it on the sheet) are the deep blocks 62, 63 and 64 cut by Yorke Avenue and Myrtle Avenue, with Emerald Avenue along the left edge; on its west side (below) are blocks 23, 27, 31, 35 and 39 divided by 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues and by narrow 20 ft alleys, with the land beyond marked vacant. The double track of the West Jersey Railroad (W.J.R.R.) crosses the top of the sheet, and a small block beyond it at the top edge is partly drawn. Building is light: two-storey frame dwellings along both sides of Yorke Avenue and Broadway, with a general store, two groceries and a tin smith on Broadway, a carpenter's shop and stables behind the Broadway frontage, and the works of J. Reese, goldbeater, on the west side of Broadway, annotated 'Admission Refused'. Most of the large interior lots are empty. House numbers along Broadway run from 1501 to 1532. Adjoining areas are on sheets 16 (Emerald Avenue side) and 18 (1st Avenue side). The sheet carries the draftsman's note 'Mae 1.1.90'.
notes: Yorke Avenue is today's York Avenue; Myrtle Avenue is today's Myrtle Street.
1st Avenue at Broadway is today part of Sunset Boulevard; modern 1st Avenue begins west of it.
Modern Park Boulevard follows the drawn West Jersey Railroad line, within 1 to 2 m.
Pearl Avenue, between Emerald and York Avenues today, is not drawn (block 62 is undivided).
The printed north arrow is about 6 degrees anticlockwise of the fitted north; probably magnetic.
Every control point lies on Broadway, so the placement is a helmert (position, scale and rotation only).

Printed sheet 17 of the Cape May series (W. Cape May N.J.), 50 ft to an inch, north about 95 deg anticlockwise (to the left); the printed arrow is about 6 deg further anticlockwise, probably magnetic. One part: both sides of Broadway from Emerald Av to 1st Av, with Yorke and Myrtle Avs on the east side and 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avs on the west, and the W.J.R.R. along the top. Every junction is on Broadway, so the fit is a helmert; the drawn railroad lies within 1 to 2 m of modern Park Boulevard (former right of way), which confirms the placement.
